label: Abstract as the value of an…: An object is abstract iff it is the value of an abstraction…
term: abstract as the value of an abstraction function (rival criterion)
definition: An object is abstract iff it is the value of an abstraction function: a generating function f with an equivalence relation R such that f(x) = f(y) iff R x y lies in f's nature (the Way of Abstraction, Hale/Wright and its metaphysical transposition via Fine's essence). It is a sibling sense, not the adopted one, and has no Lean declaration: it would need essence and abstraction-function vocabulary the corpus lacks.
note:
SEP 'Abstract Objects' §6 (navigation). The SEP notes that this account says nothing about spatial location or causal relations, so it cannot carry the owner's causal principle. Blocker for encoding: an essence ('lies in the nature of') primitive and abstraction-function vocabulary.

Declaration-completion audit (2026-11-09, analytical, attribution deferred): CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_1 remains unfinished and its allowance is retained. The missing semantics is not merely a function with an equivalence kernel. For any supplied f : A -> B, equality of outputs already induces an equivalence relation on A; Set.range f describes its values. An existential choice of such f and its kernel would admit every b : B via the constant function from Unit, including a productive causal bearer. That cannot distinguish abstraction from arbitrary generation. For a supplied Setoid on A, Quotient.mk supplies a genuine class-generating body and the quotient equality criterion, but still does not interpret why this equation lies in the generating function's nature. Reuse the standard Equivalence/Setoid/Quotient and Set.range interfaces for this mathematical part, rather than duplicating them. TruthCore.Space.IdentityCriteria.QuotientIdentity concerns spatial orbit identity, not abstraction in the present sense; TruthCore.Greek.Plato.Forms.EssentialCharacterization uses a supplied Essentially predicate for Forms and does not interpret constitutive essence of a function. Neither is a completion of this definition.

Conditional candidate fork, not the original sense: (1) a world-indexed family of generating functions whose kernels match a fixed relation at every admissible world tests necessary coextension only; equivalence with constitutive essence requires an explicit bridge and fixed-domain/function-identity policies; (2) a function specified by quotient formation and representative-independent elimination gives a positive mathematical account of class generation, but identifying that construction with metaphysical essence remains an explicit bridge. A bare Essential flag, an alias of the kernel equation, or a necessary-coextension predicate cannot complete the original. The initial modal/quotient proposals in this audit were unverified specifications; the later follow-up below records the separate quotient candidate certification.

Root connection plan: compare this rival against the adopted HasEsseInRe criterion at the existing owner causal-power/activity commitment. To count a productive bearer as abstract under this rival requires that SAME bearer's identity as a value of an admissible essentially generative abstraction; to contradict the owner's commitment additionally requires a bridge from that rival classification to EsseAbstract (no esse in re). To transfer causal inertness requires a separate prohibition of power/outgoing productive causation for those values; a kernel equality supplies neither. Incoming causation, spatiotemporal occupation, mental dependence, actual existence and necessity are also not consequences of the quotient construction. Existing esse dichotomy, Anchors and maximality aliases are unchanged. The original constitutive option remains blocked on a substantive semantics and admissibility/identity policy; the separately authorized quotient candidate is examined below. No premise discharge or declaration completion is claimed. Authorized quotient-candidate follow-up: the separate CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_9 now has a faithful quotient-presentation interpretation and checked consequences/controls in specs/quotient-generation.toml.
